This Bail Application is filed under Section 482 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS),
2023.
2. The petitioner is an accused in Crime No.572/2024 of Hill Palace Police Station, Ernakulam.

The above case is registered against the petitioner alleging offences punishable under Sections 376,
376AB, 376(2)(k), 376(2)(n) of Indian Penal Code and under Sections 3(b), 4(2), 5l, 5n, 6(l) of Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 (POCSO).
3.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner married the 2nd respondent on 29.09.2014.
The petitioner got a job in Kerala Head Load Workers Welfare Board, Ernakulam in the 2025:KER:1447 year 2016.

entities.text: Kerala Head Load Workers Welfare Board, Ernakulam
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The 2nd respondent joined to Post Graduation at Coimbatore.
Subsequently, there was some matrimonial disputes between the petitioner and the 2nd respondent.
The petitioner filed an application before the Family Court for divorce and custody of the children.
Subsequently, there was a settlement and the matter was settled.
Again the petitioner and the 2nd respondent with children started to stay together.
Again dispute arises.
Ultimately, the petitioner again filed a second divorce petition.
Thereafter, a complaint is filed against the petitioner alleging that the petitioner committed sexual offence against the 6 year old child of his own.
The case is registered as Crime No.572/2024 by the Hill Palace Police, Thripunithura.
Hence, it is alleged that the accused committed the offence.
4. Heard the learned counsel appearing for 2025:KER:1447 the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
Since the offence under Section 376AB is alleged, this Court issued notice to the victim.
The 2 nd respondent appeared through her lawyer.
5. This Court directed the learned Public Prosecutor to produce the case diary in this case.
This Court perused the case diary also.
6. It is an admitted fact that there was matrimonial dispute pending between the petitioner and the 2nd respondent.
Originally, the matter was settled and a settlement agreement was entered between Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 8 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85261353/
2 the parties as evident by Annexure-B.
Subsequently again there arises disputes.
The petitioner filed a divorce petition.
Then only the present complaint of sexual harassment is alleged.
It is true that some statement is given by the victim to the Police and also to the learned Magistrate.

But,
2025:KER:1447 this Court perused Psychological Evaluation Report submitted by the Clinical Psychologist attached to Women and Children Development Department, District Child Protection Unit.

entities.text: Women and Children Development Department, District Child Protection Unit
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
After evaluating the child the clinical psychologist observed that "as a clinician, I felt that, it is a fabricated case as child cannot answer the questions explicitly."
7.
The counsel for the 2nd respondent submitted that, there is a bar in granting bail to the petitioner under Section 438(4).

But, this Court in XXXX v. State of Kerala [2023(6) KHC 158] observed that the exclusion clause under Section 438(4) cannot be treated as applicable when no case is made out or allegations are patently false or motivated.

entities.text: XXXX v. State of Kerala [2023(6) KHC 158]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: After going through the psychological evaluation report, I think, the petitioner can be released on bail after imposing stringent conditions.
Moreover, it is a well accepted principle that the bail is the rule and the jail is the exception.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Chidambaram.

P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870],
after considering all the earlier judgments, observed that, the basic jurisprudence relating to bail remains the same inasmuch as the grant of bail is the rule and refusal is the exception so as to ensure that the accused has the opportunity of securing fair trial.

entities.text: P v Directorate of Enforcement [2019 (16) SCALE 870]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
9. Recently the Apex Court in Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
considered the point in detail.

entities.text: Siddharth v State of Uttar Pradesh and Another [2021(5)KHC 353]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paragraph of the above judgment is extracted hereunder.
"12. We may note that personal liberty is an important aspect of our constitutional mandate.

The occasion to arrest an accused during investigation arises when custodial investigation 2025:KER:1447 becomes necessary or it is a heinous crime or where there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses or accused may abscond.
Merely because an arrest can be made because it is lawful does not mandate that arrest must be made.
A distinction must be made between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercise of it.
(Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981))

entities.text: Joginder Kumar v. State of UP and Others (1994 KHC 189: (1994) 4 SCC 260: 1994 (1) KLT 919: 1994 (2) KLJ 97: AIR 1994 SC 1349: 1994 CriLJ 1981)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If arrest is made routine, it can cause incalculable harm to the reputation and self-esteem of a person.

If the Investigating Officer has no reason to believe that the accused will abscond or disobey summons and has, in fact,
throughout cooperated with the investigation we fail to appreciate why there should be a compulsion on the officer to arrest the accused."

10. In Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961], the Apex Court observed that, even if the allegation is one of grave economic offence, it is not a rule that bail should be denied in every case.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia v. Central Bureau of Investigation [2023 KHC 6961]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

Considering the dictum laid down in the above decisions and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Bail Application is allowed with the following directions:
1.
The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer within two weeks from today and shall undergo interrogation.
The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer two days consecutively from 10.00 AM to 04.00 PM after surrender.

2. After interrogation, if the Investigating Officer propose to arrest the petitioner, he shall be released on bail on executing a bond for a sum of Rs.50,000/-(Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum to the satisfaction of the arresting officer concerned.
3. The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer for interrogation as and 2025:KER:1447 when required.

The petitioner shall co- operate with the investigation and shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer.
4. Petitioner shall not leave India without permission of the jurisdictional Court.

5. Petitioner shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected,
of the commission of which he is suspected.

6. Needless to mention, it would be well within the powers of the investigating officer to investigate the matter and, if necessary, to effect recoveries on the information, if any, given by the petitioner even while the petitioner is on bail as laid down by the 2025:KER:1447 Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663].
7.

entities.text: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi) and another [2020 (1) KHC 663]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If any of the above conditions are violated by the petitioner the jurisdictional Court can cancel the bail in accordance to law, even though this bail is granted by this Court.
The prosecution and the victim are at liberty to approach the jurisdictional Court to cancel the bail, if any of the above conditions are violated.
